ai-automation-services-kit: Separate customer evidence from assumptions before buying tools.
Define the pilot scope, reviewer, exclusions and stop conditions.
Pass all six fictional demo events and a visible failure/retry check without sending messages.
Verify setup and monthly costs without confusing them with price or profit.
Draft a proposal without invented clients, testimonials or guaranteed returns.
Document the off switch, manual fallback, data handling and review decision.
ai-prompt-pack: Choose one small task you do every week.
Pick a prompt template and replace the bracketed details with your own.
Try the prompt with an AI tool; do not include passwords or private information.
Ask for one change, such as a shorter or clearer answer, and check the final result.
Save the prompt that worked best so you can reuse it.
automation-kit: List a few tasks you repeat every week.
Choose one task that is frequent and frustrating.
Write down its trigger, action, and desired result.
Build the workflow one step at a time and test each step.
Run a complete test with sample information before turning it on.
Add a failure notification and review the run history after the first day.
coding-basics-kit: Choose a beginner-friendly coding tool and create a small practice project.
Create a variable and print its value.
Write an if/else condition and try it with different values.
Use a loop to process a short list of values.
Write a function that takes input and returns a result.
Complete one practice task from the Coding Basics Kit.
Build a tiny project, run it yourself, and explain what each part does.
Put your project in a Git repository and save a commit.
Ask an AI assistant to explain one function line by line, then rewrite it yourself.
ml-workbook: Choose a beginner dataset, such as Iris or Titanic, and note where it came from.
Write down the question you want your model to answer.
Identify the features and the label, and check for missing or duplicated data.
Create a simple baseline prediction to compare against.
Train a simple model and evaluate it on data it did not train on.
Inspect several incorrect predictions and note any patterns.
Record the model, score, and what you learned; consider what could go wrong if it is inaccurate.
productivity-boost: Choose one real task you need to finish today.
Give an AI tool the relevant context and ask it to organize or draft the work.
Review the result, correct errors, and remove anything private or confidential.
Use the reviewed result to complete your task.
Save any prompt that helped, and note one improvement for next time.
website-bundle: Write one sentence describing your website's purpose and audience.
Sketch a simple plan for the Home, About, content, and Contact pages.
Create a project with an HTML file, stylesheet, and script file.
Build a clear headline and one main action for visitors.
Add a descriptive page title, image alt text, and a way to contact you.
Check the site on a narrow/mobile-sized screen and test every link.
Publish the site, open the live URL, and ask one person what was confusing.
design-starter-kit: Write one sentence describing who the design is for and what it should do.
Collect three examples you like and note what works about each.
Sketch your idea on paper first, in at least two versions.
Build a simple prototype in your chosen tool.
Check contrast, text size and spacing.
Show it to one person and write down their feedback.
Make one improvement based on that feedback.
app-launch-kit: Write the problem your app solves in one sentence.
List features and keep only the one that matters most.
Sketch the main screens on paper.
Build the core feature first, and commit your work often.
Test it yourself with unusual inputs, such as empty or very long text.
Ask a friend to try it and watch where they get stuck.
Publish it and write down your next three improvements.
Ask an AI assistant to review your code for bugs, and verify its suggestions by running them.
ai-coding-prompts: Pick one small task and write it as a clear prompt with input and expected output.
Ask the assistant to explain its code before you run it.
Run the code and check the result against your expectation.
Ask for edge cases and test at least two of them.
Ask for a code review and apply one change yourself.
Rewrite one generated function in your own words.
Save a commit describing what you built and learned.
content-creator-kit: Choose one topic you know well and one audience.
Ask an AI assistant for 10 ideas and pick the easiest one.
Draft the text or script, then rewrite it in your own voice.
Add one visual, voice-over or short video, using only content you are allowed to use.
Check facts, names and licences, and keep private information out.
Publish or save it, then note what worked for next time.
origin-analysis-kit: Write your analysis question in one sentence.
Create or anonymise practice data before using any AI assistant.
Import the data and fill in column names and units.
Plot the data and add a reference line at your target.
Calculate the mean, standard deviation and CV %.
Check your result by hand or with a second method before reporting it.
data-visualization-kit: Write one question your chart should answer.
Check that rows, columns, labels and units are consistent.
Choose a chart type that fits the question.
Create the chart and label axes, units and sample size.
Check the graph against the source data and note one limitation.
research-prompt-kit: Narrow your topic to one neutral, answerable question.
Find and open at least two original sources.
Record claims, exact evidence, dates and limitations in a table.
Ask AI to synthesize only the evidence you provide.
Verify every citation and follow your institution's AI-use rules.
ai-for-education-kit: Check school, age and course rules before using a tool.
Never upload identifying or sensitive student information.
Use AI for a lesson draft, practice or tutoring hints, not final judgement.
Verify facts, answers, accessibility and suitability before sharing.
ai-website-kit: Write a one-paragraph brief: who the site is for and what one action visitors should take.
Never paste passwords, API keys or private customer data into an AI builder or chat.
Open the draft on your phone and on a computer and fix anything that overflows or is hard to read.
Check headings, link text, image descriptions and colour contrast before publishing.
Confirm every claim, price and contact detail is true, and that you have the right to use each image.
Open the live website on your phone, test its main action, save a backup and record one improvement from feedback.
advanced-measurement-analysis-kit: Write the question, units, measurement window and approved limits before calculating.
Keep an untouched raw export and record instrument and calibration context.
Check missing values, duplicate timestamps, sampling intervals and flagged rows without silently deleting data.
Summarise pump stability by pre-defined time windows and compare the results with the raw trace.
Confirm whether scanner values are thickness or areal mass loading; use only a validated conversion.
Compare independent runs at the run level, not as though every reading were an independent run.
Save analysis code or project, document exclusions, and independently verify key results.
ai-workflows-kit: Write the goal, trigger, steps, reviewer and stop rules before building.
Decide which steps change something and require human approval.
Test with sample data and a test account before connecting real ones.
Give least access, set run or spending limits and know how to switch it off.
Treat text from emails and web pages as data, never as instructions.
Review runs, corrections and time saved after a week.
advanced-web-dev-kit: Write a one-page spec with at most three must-do items and a check for each.
Commit to Git before the AI changes anything; use one branch per feature.
Ask for one small change at a time and name the files it may edit.
Write tests first and never let the AI weaken them.
Read the diff for secrets, new dependencies and unchecked input before committing.
Deploy from main with secrets in environment variables and check the live site.
advanced-no-code-kit: Map the trigger, data, decisions, actions and owner before building.
Check required fields and formats in the first step and stop with a clear message.
Give every possible input a path, including a default one for review.
Use an event ID or lookup step so repeats do not create duplicates.
Set retries, an error route and an alert that reaches a real person.
Write a runbook and review run history every week.
ai-small-business-kit: Define one offer and a customer question without inventing research.
Collect feedback with permission and remove identifying details before using AI.
Check every product claim against your actual offer.
Verify FAQ answers and route unknown questions to a person.
Approve one campaign draft and record results without promising sales.
ai-video-creation-kit: Write a single-message brief and a timed storyboard.
Record permission or licensing for every clip, voice and music track.
Review generated footage for distortions and misleading claims.
Correct captions and check the video with sound off on a phone.
Check current platform AI disclosure rules before publishing.
ai-career-skills-kit: Choose a real role and match its requirements to verifiable experience.
Remove personal identifiers before uploading drafts to an AI service.
Tailor your resume without invented skills, dates or results.
Practise interview answers using real examples and your own words.
Review each application yourself and record a next action.
ai-spreadsheets-kit: Keep an unchanged Raw sheet and a separate Working copy.
Check five unique IDs, one missing quantity and one known zero.
Verify the row results: 10, 6, 5, 0 and REVIEW.
Reconcile the known subtotal of 21 and the one unresolved row.
Label the chart honestly without presenting unknown values as zero.
Save notes and recheck all formulas after reopening the workbook.
